title: New CTA Index being revealed! - Systematic Investor 311

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/New CTA Index being revealed! - Systematic Investor 311.docx

speakers: Andrew Beer (managing member, DBi / replication ETF manager)
summary: Systematic Investor 311 (Sep 2024): Andrew Beer on August 2024 whipsaws, a 10-factor weekly replication of the SG CTA Index (unchanged since 2016, ~300bp edge, 90% correlation), allocator resistance to trend, and the new SG CTA Investable Hedge Fund Index built on his methodology.

coverage.note: Intro, small talk on media and AI summarization: nothing actionable
Performance data; whipsaw drivers and three shifts
Short vs long-term models, replication limitations (DBMF question)
Fixed model since 2016, 300bp and 90% correlation, why 10 factors work
Correlation monitoring, index not investable, allocation size
Fee crystallisation, interest income in composites, replication rationale
Replicator risk, failed replication, bottom-up vs top-down
Partnering, SG CTA and Trend index construction
Why hedge fund indices exist and their problems
SG CTA Investable index, backtest dial-turning
Idiosyncratic risk, fee arbitrage, industry size

completeness_estimate: 0.89 - first reader covered the August 2024 review, replication method, fee/correlation numbers, allocator-psychology and index-launch themes closely; missed the BoJ reaction function, the industry-wide pattern point, the 300bp-not-constant caveat, the 5% allocation claim, and Andrew's distinction between a one-week replication bet and a real trend model.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: equities clearly it's been a challenge to navigate this kind of v-shaped uh trip we've had
claims.claim: August 2024 was a down month for CTAs: V-shaped equities (Japan not fully recovered), JGBs, non-US fixed income and energies were hard, softs and grains and gold were decent.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it's in a 10.5% draw down since its high in in March that's about 50% of its worst draw down
claims.claim: The SG Trend Index was in a 10.5% drawdown from its March high, about half its worst drawdown, so August 2024 was not catastrophic.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: beat of 50 right now down 1.68% in August up 3.43% uh this year
claims.claim: Performance data to late Aug 2024: BTOP50 -1.68% in August (+3.43% YTD), SG CTA -2.58% (+2% YTD), SG Trend -3.63% (+2.22%), STI +0.19%, versus MSCI World +14.6% and S&P 500 +18.3% YTD; Trend barometer 59.
claims.indicator: BTOP50, SG CTA, SG Trend, STI

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: how much of it is rational repricing of assets based upon changes in underlying fundamental economic or macroeconomic conditions and how much of it is the technical stuff
claims.claim: In big market whipsaws you cannot tell in real time how much is rational repricing versus technical liquidation feedback; fundamental traders change their views as prices move because they assume someone knows something.
claims.testable: no: not testable in real time

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: there were three really really really big shifts
claims.claim: Mid-July to early August 2024: Trump's rising odds and pressure off Biden, growth fine so no Fed cut before the election, and BoJ only making noises; all three reversed within two weeks, producing the whipsaw.
claims.indicator: US election odds, Fed expectations, BoJ policy

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: short-term models sound great but they're much more at risk of getting ferociously whipsawed in three days like that
claims.claim: Short-term trend models are more at risk of being whipsawed by sharp three-day repricing and missing the mild recovery.
claims.testable: yes: short vs long lookback in whipsaw episodes

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: a replication model or a long-term Trend follower will be slower to drisk during that period of time
claims.claim: Long-term trend and replication models are slower to derisk if the August move proved to be an inflection point (as November 2023), costing more in that case.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: the idea that the market is going to tell you when you're wrong and you're going to get out of a trade is not something that fits into the standard ethos of a an alpha generating hedge fund investment
claims.claim: Trend following's exit-on-loss ethos conflicts with the hedge-fund allocator view that managers should have conviction, a barrier to allocation.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: there are two no limitations of replication one is sometimes we're going to miss trades
claims.claim: Replication has two limitations: it misses some trades (Jan-Feb 2023) and is slower at inflection points; 2023 was the only year it underperformed the index.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: incentive fees smooth returns
claims.claim: Because a replicator charges no incentive fees, it looks more volatile than the net-of-fee index it is compared with; fee and expense intermediation provides a tailwind.
claims.testable: yes: fee model of index returns

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: multiple CT came out proclaiming that
claims.claim: In Jan-Feb 2023 several CTAs claimed replication only worked in 2019-2022 due to specific macro conditions and would fail; the author rebuts it.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: in our models we use 10 factors you know big obvious factors two t and 30 years in treasuries
claims.claim: The replication model uses 10 factors: 2y/10y/30y Treasuries, three equity indices, euro, yen, gold and oil, estimated from recent CTA index returns and implemented each Monday.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: you're making a onewe bet that you're you're sufficiently accurate there
claims.claim: Replication is a one-week bet that is self-correcting over time if slightly wrong, with simplicity contrasting the increasing complexity of actual funds.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: there's this conflation of complexity therefore justifying higher fees
claims.claim: Complexity (many instruments) is claimed to give better diversification and alpha and so justify higher fees, but there is little data behind it.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: July 2016 to the present we've been running these rep replication models that haven't changed
claims.claim: The replication models have run unchanged since July 2016, with a very high bar for changes, unlike other quant strategies.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: we've done about 300 basis points better than the broad industry with a 90% correlation
claims.claim: Since 2016 the replicator beat the CTA index by about 300bp a year at 90% correlation through fee and expense disintermediation and about 10bp annual trading costs.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: most millions of different factors equities Etc over a short period of time can be boiled down to a handful of large liquid instruments
claims.claim: Over a one-week window most CTA exposures reduce to a handful of large liquid instruments (10-year Treasury has gravitational pull), capturing about 90% of what they do.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: like Coco we would say is really idiosyncratic
claims.claim: Idiosyncratic markets such as cocoa are missed by the replicator, producing multi-week tracking gaps like Jan-Feb 2023, but this is not a structural failure.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: 2016 through the end of 2022 was some bizarre period where the Fed was dominating markets
claims.claim: Critics argued that 2016-22 was a Fed-dominated period of tightly linked instruments, after which idiosyncratic dispersion would produce unreplicable alpha; the replicator's results contradicted this.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: shorter term models were great in on November 1st last year and they were great on March 13th of of last year
claims.claim: Shorter-term models benefited from violent prolonged whipsaws on 1 Nov 2023 and 13 Mar 2023 while slower models and replication were hurt at reversals.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: I don't see it in the numbers there's no evidence for that
claims.claim: Trading hundreds of markets is not shown to be better than trading 60 in the data; 10-15 markets may suffice.
claims.testable: yes: test performance by market count

correction.issue: Over-states the host's view: he says there is no evidence that hundreds of markets beat 60, but explicitly disclaims knowing whether 10-15 markets are equivalent ('I don't have enough knowledge or data'), speaking as a hypothetical CTA.
correction.fix: The host, role-playing a CTA, agrees there is no evidence in the numbers that trading hundreds of markets beats trading about 60, but says he lacks the data to say that 10-15 markets would be equivalent; the replicator's results suggest you can get quite far with few.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: the data the data is there right you you add more instruments you get more diversification
claims.claim: Adding instruments does increase diversification, but unlike a stock picker's best ideas, managed futures is a series of small-edge bets (52-55% hit rate).

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: if you're flipping coins every week there will be periods of time where you flip five tailes in a row
claims.claim: Rolling replication correlation to the CTA index varies but does not fall to 20%, because the weekly fit is self-correcting; streaks of misses are expected.
claims.indicator: rolling correlation to SG CTA Index

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: we're trying to track something that we cannot invest in directly
claims.claim: The CTA index cannot be invested in directly; allocating to 20 managers at full fees or choosing a few funds are alternatives, hence replication.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: man will tell you that it should be 40% of your portfolio and a lot of guys in you know on fin twit will say it should be a minimum of 25% of your portfolio
claims.claim: Claims on optimal CTA allocation range from 25% to 40% (Man, social media), while Winton says other considerations matter.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: a lot of managers also have quarterly crystallization so it didn't help them
claims.claim: In 2024 many managers made new highs early so performance fees kicked in, and with quarterly crystallisation no fees came back in Q2, so replicators with no incentive fee outperform in such years.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: not all managers in include interest income in their composite returns
claims.claim: Some managers exclude interest income from composite returns, so the SG index may not include much interest while replication products do, mixing apples with apples of a different colour.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: I want liquidity and you know and ideally you know put in some sort of a rapper
claims.claim: Replication is not perfect, but to get exposure to the space with less manager risk, liquidity and a wrapper nothing better has been found.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: you could have something in the model that goes out of sync for a while
claims.claim: Replicator risk exists alongside manager risk: the model can go out of sync or have a bug.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: only replicate funds with sharp ratios of 2.5 or higher right with a factor model with daily liquidity that's that's predictably stupid
claims.claim: A late-2000s bank replicated only funds with Sharpe above 2.5 using a daily-liquidity factor model and ended up holding every mortgage-backed securities fund, showing naive replication fails.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: the bottomup models you know which are supposed to add a meaningful amount of value
claims.claim: Bottom-up replication (calls on moving-average crossovers per market) does not add value over simple top-down models, though new entrants (KFA, Alpha Simplex ETF) may add some.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: fund selection hedge fund selection as a practical matter is an utterly efficient process
claims.claim: Hedge fund selection is information-efficient and subject to selection bias: allocators see funds only after success.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: manures have hit the trifecta of what a hedge fund is supposed to be low correlation to to equities
claims.claim: Over the past 10 years managed futures hit the hedge fund trifecta (low correlation to equities, does well when needed, high alpha), yet are only 6% of hedge fund allocations.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: it's not that they believe it hasn't worked it's that they believe it shouldn't work
claims.claim: Allocators doubt trend following because they are trained to believe in skill and information edge, so the evidence of 24 years is dismissed.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: there's no special information we're all looking at the or you guys are all looking at the same return streams
claims.claim: Trend following has no special information: trades are in plain sight and exits come when the market 'slaps you in the face'.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: an economic transfer of wealth between uh from commercial players to to speculators
claims.claim: Mal Lucas's explanation for futures returns is an economic transfer from commercial hedgers to speculators, a risk-premium rationale.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: as their anxiety goes up they feel compelled to look and look and look and look and look
claims.claim: Allocator anxiety about trend following leads them to focus on headcount and organisation rather than the model.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: an index of the equally weighted Neta Fe returns of the 20 largest manag creaters hedge funds
claims.claim: The SG CTA Index is the equal-weighted net-fee return of the 20 largest open CTAs since January 2000, reconstituted each January, with daily data and little selection bias.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: the trend index is like 1.3 times the first version with a 98% correlation
claims.claim: The SG Trend Index (10 trend-heavy of the 20) is about 1.3 times the CTA index with 98% correlation, with more leverage, higher return and larger drawdowns.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: this is called a capital markets assumption and it is the found Foundation upon which you run your model to decide how much
claims.claim: Hedge fund indices serve as long-term track record for capital market assumptions in allocation and for manager benchmarking.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: when you pick the index product you're never wrong because there is no manager selection risk
claims.claim: Allocators prefer index products because they never face manager selection risk; hedge fund indices are net of fees and not investable, unlike equity indices.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: socken has launched something called the soj CTA investable hedge fund index
claims.claim: SG launched the CTA Investable Hedge Fund Index based on the replication model, backtested to 2002 and available on Bloomberg.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: people sit in the room and they turn dials
claims.claim: Index backtests suffer from dial-turning (alternative risk premia were built by quants tuning rebalancing and definitions), so long backtests of new indices need Caveat Emptor; this one rests on eight years of live unchanged model.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: the idiocratic risk of what we're doing
claims.claim: Replicator idiosyncratic risk versus the SG CTA Index is much less than single-manager risk, though not zero.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: what we're trying to do synthetically through fee Arbitrage
claims.claim: Institutional allocators often pay less than full fees and thus beat the CTA index; fee disintermediation in an investable index (hundreds of bp better) could support larger allocations.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: the mutual fund space which has been around for 15 years is $20 billion
claims.claim: The managed futures industry has about $300bn; the mutual fund version is $20bn and Corey Hoffstein's return-stacked ETFs near $1bn of a $10 trillion market.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: back then the industry as a whole was less than 10 billion at least now we're up to 400 billion
claims.claim: Managed futures industry assets grew from under $10bn to about $400bn, host's recollection.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: except with a small issue that you know they risk dropping uh you know sort of torching their their their tastic Market
claims.claim: The Bank of Japan had been reluctant to tighten because a stronger yen would risk torching the Japanese stock market, which was doing well on a weak yen and exports; this constraint is why markets treated BoJ talk as noise until it suddenly acted in August 2024.
claims.conditions: BoJ tightening is limited while a weak yen supports the equity market
claims.testable: partly - policy reaction function, one episode

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: it's an industrywide issue um it's not it's not as though the industry is up 20% and we're up three
claims.claim: The smooth-uptrend-then-sharp-reversal pattern in recent years is a feature of the whole managed futures industry, not a replicator flaw, and since the third-quarter 2022 peak the replicator, though in drawdown, is still ahead of the hedge fund index.
claims.indicator: DBMF vs SG CTA Index since Q3 2022 peak
claims.testable: yes - compare drawdown paths of replicator and index

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: you can see there's been a ton of whips saws you know syncratic whipsaws spread across a lot of these other instruments
claims.claim: Diversified trend models are used as risk-management tools, and in the recent period many idiosyncratic whipsaws across the instruments the 10-factor replicator does not hold explain why a simple replica can beat the more diversified CTA index in a given year.
claims.conditions: years with many idiosyncratic reversals outside the core liquid contracts
claims.testable: partly - needs contribution analysis by instrument

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: if you look at the past couple of years it hasn't been 300 basis points of of of outperformance
claims.claim: The roughly 300bp annual edge of the replicator over the index is a long-run average, not something to expect every year; in the last couple of years the outperformance was smaller, so the right question is how much to expect, not whether replication works.
claims.indicator: replicator minus SG CTA Index excess return
claims.conditions: edge depends on fee and expense disintermediation plus tracking noise
claims.testable: yes - rolling excess return of replicator over index

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: as a onewe bet which is what replication is on the broad exposures of the space um I feel confident that 10 yeah I think that's fine
claims.claim: A very simple 10-instrument trend model is not the ideal way to run a trend-following business, but as a one-week bet on the broad exposures of the CTA space, 10 liquid instruments suffice; so few markets work for replication, not for a real trend system.
claims.conditions: holds for tracking an index over one week, not for generating trend returns directly
claims.testable: yes - replication fit versus number of instruments

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: it's an absolutely no-brainer that this should be maybe not 40% but but but 5% of every single portfolio and they don't do it
claims.claim: Given 24 years of SG CTA Index data, at least a 5% allocation to managed futures in every portfolio is a no-brainer, well below the 25-40% some propose, yet allocators do not do it.
claims.indicator: SG CTA Index since 2000; portfolio allocation weight
claims.testable: yes - portfolio optimisation with the index history

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: they hope it doesn't work because they somehow have economic skin in the game
claims.claim: Part of allocator and industry resistance to trend following and replication is motivated: those with an economic stake in stock picking or higher-fee products hope it does not work because it is disruptive and threatening, on top of the belief that it should not work.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: there are a few extra uh independent checks and balances uh each day
claims.claim: Daily-liquidity regulated wrappers (UCITS, US ETFs) bring extra independent checks and let investors exit quickly, so allocators run lighter and shorter due diligence on them than on hedge funds.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: let's hope not everybody goes into Trend following and ctas that might make it more difficult for us
claims.claim: If assets in trend following keep growing, crowding could make trend following harder, even though the industry (about $300-400bn) is still small relative to the potential.
claims.conditions: when trend-following assets become a large share of market flows
claims.testable: partly - needs capacity and flow data
